title: QUIC Connection Migration Hosted Proof Lane Verification
verification_method: Requirement-home tests, helper dry-run planning, workflow review, artifact inspection, and hosted workflow dispatch when external evidence is required.
preconditions: The external `quic-interop-runner` checkout includes `ngtcp2`, `quiche`, `aioquic`, `picoquic`, `lsquic`, `quic-go`, `msquic`, `quinn`, and `neqo` peer slots.
Hosted dispatch has Docker Engine 28.1 or later, Python 3.12, and Wireshark packet-analysis tools available.
The repo-local helper remains responsible for image replacement, runner invocation, inventory output, and per-cell artifact capture.
scope: Verify that the repository exposes manual advisory hosted proof lanes for server-role connectionmigration against ngtcp2 using the neqo slot, plus a blocked comparison lane for lsquic, quiche, quic-go, msquic, and aioquic, without promoting blocked cells or changing ordinary CI gates.
procedure: Review `.github/workflows/interop-runner-handshake.yml` and confirm the `connectionmigration-server-proof` and `connectionmigration-server-proof-blocked` profiles are `workflow_dispatch` only.
Confirm the proof profile includes a server-role matrix cell against `ngtcp2` using the `neqo` slot for `connectionmigration`.
Confirm the blocked profile includes server-role matrix cells against `lsquic`, `quiche`, `quic-go`, `msquic`, and `aioquic` for `connectionmigration`.
Confirm every matrix cell invokes `scripts/interop/Invoke-QuicInteropRunner.ps1` with matrix-provided role, local implementation slot, peer slot, testcase, timeout, and artifact root.
Confirm each cell uploads a distinct artifact bundle with `if: always()`.
Run the focused requirement-home tests for `REQ-QUIC-INT-0018` and `REQ-QUIC-INT-0022`.
Run representative helper dry-run plans for the server-role ngtcp2 connectionmigration cell using the `neqo` slot, plus the blocked comparison peers.

When external evidence is required, dispatch `gh workflow run interop-runner-handshake.yml --repo incursa/quic-dotnet --ref main -f coverage_profile=connectionmigration-server-proof` and `gh workflow run interop-runner-handshake.yml --repo incursa/quic-dotnet --ref main -f coverage_profile=connectionmigration-server-proof-blocked` and inspect each uploaded `runner-report.json` plus selected output logs.
expected_result: The repository configuration provides opt-in hosted proof lanes that can collect per-cell artifacts for Incursa.Quic as the server role against ngtcp2 using the neqo slot for the connectionmigration proof cells, while keeping a blocked comparison lane for lsquic, quiche, quic-go, msquic, and aioquic, and keeping the major-peer-matrix profile and HTTP/3 out of scope.
status_summary: Planned for hosted execution. The repository now has split connectionmigration proof lanes and the helper inventory already classifies connectionmigration as supported/executed. The latest hosted picoquic attempt was rejected because the runner could not validate the image signature, so the proof lane is being retargeted to ngtcp2 while the blocked comparison lane keeps lsquic, quiche, quic-go, msquic, and aioquic visible. Full SpecTrace core validation remains blocked by the current baseline and is not claimed as passing by this artifact.

supplemental_sections.heading: Deferred Coverage
supplemental_sections.content: `http3` remains out of scope. `v2`, `rebind-port`, and `rebind-addr` remain prerequisite-blocked under the non-HTTP/3 inventory. `connectionmigration` now has hosted proof lanes against ngtcp2 using the neqo slot plus a blocked comparison lane against lsquic, quiche, quic-go, msquic, and aioquic, and the proof lanes are being refreshed because the latest hosted picoquic attempt was rejected by the runner's image-signature validation rather than being claimed green.
